Przemysl New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Przemyśl, Poland

Not demolished. One of the few Jewish cemeteries in Poland still active today, this site was founded around 1847 after the older Przemyśl cemetery filled up. It holds numerous Holocaust monuments and victims' graves, including a postwar memorial 'in memory of 4,000 Jews, victims of Nazi crimes in 1939-1944' near the entrance gate; a mass grave for Jews from Medyka murdered by Germans in 1943; and a symbolic grave for social activist Captain Emil Klausner, murdered by the NKVD at Katyn. Twelve mass graves in the cemetery's central section hold German execution victims from Przemyśl, Stalowa Wola, Lubaczów, and elsewhere. It entered Poland's monument register (no. A-161) on November 3, 1986.
